title: WORD MELT
name: WORD MELT
goal: Hear one charged word as sound instead of carrying its whole story.
steps:
1. Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop there and look around the room.
5. Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.

title: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
name: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
goal: Fit the conversation to the amount you can safely handle right now.
steps:
1. Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
2. Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
3. Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
4. Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.

title: THEN AND NOW, NO STORY DETAILS
name: THEN AND NOW, NO STORY DETAILS
ritual_name: THEN AND NOW, NO STORY DETAILS
goal: Separate what happened then from the options available to you now.
steps:
1. Say, “That happened then,” without describing what happened.
2. State your exact present location and today's date.
3. Name one freedom or option available now.
4. Identify who can help in the current day.
5. End after one comparison and return to the room.
numberedSteps:
1. Say, “That happened then,” without describing what happened.
2. State your exact present location and today's date.
3. Name one freedom or option available now.
4. Identify who can help in the current day.
5. End after one comparison and return to the room.
numbered_steps:
1. Say, “That happened then,” without describing what happened.
2. State your exact present location and today's date.
3. Name one freedom or option available now.
4. Identify who can help in the current day.
5. End after one comparison and return to the room.
win: The past stayed undescribed while today's place, date, freedom, and support became explicit.
mindBend: Memory can collapse time by carrying old helplessness forward — one present option proves the conditions are not identical.
mind_bend: Memory can collapse time by carrying old helplessness forward — one present option proves the conditions are not identical.

title: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
ritual_name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
goal: Change one part of an imagined scene and see which emotion actually moves.
steps:
1. Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
2. Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
4. Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.

goal: Require each new thinking lap to produce something genuinely new.
steps:

3. Shift attention to one present sensation or practical action.

title: TELL IT AT THE SPEED OF SAFETY
name: TELL IT AT THE SPEED OF SAFETY
ritual_name: TELL IT AT THE SPEED OF SAFETY
goal: Share difficult material at a pace set by safety, facts, and the support you actually want.
steps:

title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
name: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
goal: Make fear state exactly what should happen, by when, and how confident it is.
steps:
1. Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Use the result to update confidence in either direction.

STEPS
1. Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Use the result to update confidence in either direction.

WIN
The prediction gained a visible outcome, deadline, and pre-check confidence that could later move with naturally occurring evidence.

MIND BEND
A vague fear cannot be wrong. Edges make a forecast testable enough for reality to update it.

FORMULA FLOW
Pin Forecast → Set Clock → Score Odds → Observe Safely → Update Odds

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not test danger, invade privacy, or repeat the observation to chase certainty.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
name: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
goal: Change only the quietest safe channel of body alarm and leave the louder ones alone.
steps:
1. Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.

title: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
name: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
ritual_name: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
goal: Spend one minute in direct experience without using your biography to explain who is here.
steps:
1. For sixty seconds, do not recall name, history, status, or plans.
2. Stay with changing sound, pressure, light, and movement.
3. Notice the simple ongoing sense of being present through those changes.
4. Reclaim your biography on purpose at the end.

title: RETURN THEIR ACTION; KEEP YOUR CHOICE
name: RETURN THEIR ACTION; KEEP YOUR CHOICE
ritual_name: RETURN THEIR ACTION; KEEP YOUR CHOICE
goal: Keep the other person’s behaviour, what you learned, and what you choose now in separate boxes.
steps:
1. Imagine three boxes: THE OTHER PERSON’S BEHAVIOUR; WHAT I LEARNED; WHAT I CHOOSE NOW.
2. Keep each thought in the right box.
3. Forgiveness is not required on command.
4. Take one action from the third box.
numberedSteps:
1. Imagine three boxes: THE OTHER PERSON’S BEHAVIOUR; WHAT I LEARNED; WHAT I CHOOSE NOW.
2. Keep each thought in the right box.
3. Forgiveness is not required on command.
4. Take one action from the third box.
numbered_steps:
1. Imagine three boxes: THE OTHER PERSON’S BEHAVIOUR; WHAT I LEARNED; WHAT I CHOOSE NOW.
2. Keep each thought in the right box.
3. Forgiveness is not required on command.
4. Take one action from the third box.
win: The next action came from your present choice without requiring forced forgiveness or denial of what happened.
mindBend: Letting go does not require calling the other person’s action okay. It can mean refusing to let that action choose your next move.

title: UNWIND IN REVERSE

goal: Release a tension chain in the reverse order that it built.
steps:
1. Recall which muscle group tightened last.
2. Soften it first, then work back toward the first area that braced.

4. Finish at the original starting point and compare the whole chain.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Park a problem until the missing information needed to think usefully actually exists.

STEPS
1. Name what is missing: another person’s decision, a test result, a future opening, or a resource.
2. Name what change would make thinking useful again.
3. Until that happens, store the problem with that trigger and stop working it.

WIN
The missing information got a clear reopening trigger, so the problem no longer needed constant mental work.

MIND BEND
Thinking cannot solve information that does not exist yet. Repeating the calculation only creates more versions of the same gap.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Variable → State Change → Store Away

SAFETY
PAUSE
Continue any preparation that remains possible while the variable is unavailable.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ISSUE THE DECISION RECEIPT
name: ISSUE THE DECISION RECEIPT
goal: Give a completed decision a receipt so doubt has a specific rule for reopening it.
steps:

title: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
name: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
ritual_name: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
goal: Route a returning concern to one real destination or mark it undeliverable.
steps:
1. Assign the concern to one place: a named person, calendar slot, document, task name, or deliberate release.
2. Say the address in your mind and route the thought there each time it returns.
3. If no useful address exists, mark the thought UNDELIVERABLE and let it pass without rerouting.

title: PUT THE PROMISE AT THE CROSSROADS
name: PUT THE PROMISE AT THE CROSSROADS
ritual_name: PUT THE PROMISE AT THE CROSSROADS
goal: Place one short cue exactly where you usually begin renegotiating the decision.
steps:
1. Find the exact moment where the decision usually changes direction.
2. Create a short mental cue that names the action you want there.
3. Picture reaching the crossroads and hearing the cue once.
4. When the moment arrives, use the cue before renegotiation begins.

title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
name: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
goal: Find a work-rest gear that matches actual strain instead of your prediction about strain.
steps:
1. Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.
numberedSteps:
1. Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.
numbered_steps:
1. Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.
win: A short work cycle with a deliberate ending revealed whether the next ratio should increase, hold, or finish.
mindBend: Anticipated effort and experienced effort are different measurements. Testing the gear replaces dread with data.

title: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
name: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
ritual_name: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
goal: Collapse repeated clues that all came from the same source before judging how much evidence you have.
steps:
1. Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion.
2. Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
3. Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately.
4. Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain.
numberedSteps:

mindBend: Five clues can create false confidence when they are copies of one origin. Independence matters more than raw count.

NAME THE GUARANTEE YOU ARE SECRETLY BUYING

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Name the guarantee you hope checking will give you, then ask whether information can really provide it.

STEPS
1. Finish: ‘If I keep checking, I hope to guarantee that…’.
2. Ask whether any amount of information can truly provide that promise.
3. Gather only information that could change your action. Carry the remaining uncertainty without more checking.

WIN
Useful information stayed while the impossible guarantee was recognised as something checking could not provide.

MIND BEND
Checking can promise a feeling that evidence cannot permanently deliver. That is why one more check can keep becoming another.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Guarantee → Test Promise → Gather Evidence

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not stop investigation while essential facts are still obtainable.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
name: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
ritual_name: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
goal: Use real task feedback while letting self-commentary remain faint and unanswered at the edge.
steps:
1. Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.
2. Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
3. When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
4. Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.

title: ROTATE THE OBSERVATION DECK
name: ROTATE THE OBSERVATION DECK
goal: Try three ways of paying attention before choosing the one that fits the task.
steps:
1. Notice the same moment three ways: mainly your body, mainly the environment, then both together.
2. Notice what each view shows clearly and what it misses.
3. Use the view that fits the next task best.
